utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber is aware that both parties have some preliminaries. We'll pay attention to them later, that none of them are urgent. I'd like to draw your attention to one item in relation to D557, which is MFI'd. It is the Islamic declaration of Alija Izetbegovic, and the Defence used a very small number of pages of that Islamic declaration during the testimony of Nenad Kecmanovic. The entire 77-page document was marked for identification as D557, pending an agreement between the parties about which pages of the document should be received in evidence. Subsequently, the Defence informed the Chamber that it wanted to tender the entire document. On the 13th of October, the Chamber set a one-week deadline to receive the reasons for tendering the entirety of the document. The Defence did not file any submissions in this regard, and the Chamber wonders whether it is to understand that under those circumstances the tendering of D557 is withdrawn. And that's a question to you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry that we missed the dead-line, but we do not withdraw this statement. You'll see that our incoming witnesses will discuss this document as well. And I think that we spoke with somebody from the Prosecution and that there is -- there was no objection from their side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the Chamber wanted to know why there are good reasons to tender the whole of the document. Simply we spontaneously asked for a further explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our position is that it's not possible to understand parts of that document. We should have the whole document in front of us to be able to understand the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a short explanation, Mr. Lukic. You're invited to file the submissions the Chamber requested you to file.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to complete the record, I think Mr. Lukic is correct. He'd spoken to me specifically and we'd communicated that we had no objections to it being admitted in whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's on the record. So the Chamber would like to receive submissions on the matter, Mr. Lukic, and a bit more elaborate that the one you gave a second ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djuric. You find a new face before you. The Chamber is happy that we are all three Judges here again. I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to start this morning with the topic of paramilitaries. Now, you mentioned in your statement that measures were taken against paramilitaries and I've just a few questions about that. First, before measures were taken against the paramilitaries, they were causing problems for the Serb population; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were causing problems for the Serb population and for the Bosniak Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And those included breaking into Serb houses and flats?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Included disturbing the peace generally?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. Disturbing the peace, breaking into apartments, looting, so the police within the domain of its authority and powers took all necessary measures and to that end the Crisis Staff also adopted certain instructions on forbidding any breaking into abandoned apartments and houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 51 of your statement, you're discussing parliaments and you say: "These units had become so arrogant that they did not shrink from stopping an official vehicle that transported our minister from abusing him, getting him out of the vehicle, et cetera." Now the specific paramilitary unit that did this was the Yellow Wasps, right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the minister you're referring to was Minister of the Interior Mico Stanisic, retire?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware the Yellow Wasps had also stopped and mistreated Mr. Velibor Ostojic; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct. Since Velibor Ostojic had less protection and a smaller security detail, then he was exposed to more mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to focus on the incident with Minister Stanic for a moment. You learnt about this incident in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You learned about it from his driver? Minister Stanic's driver.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it had happened either the same day or the day before you that learned about it?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now among other things you were told to get the police ready and expect an order, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the order to conduct an operation against the Yellow Wasps was issued a day or two later; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the Vlasenica SJB's relationship with the army. To start, the JNA's Novi Sad Corps left Vlasenica on or around the 19th of May, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The order was that the former JNA had to leave the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the 19th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, when they left they left behind equipment and armoured personnel carriers; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the equipment stayed behind. I don't know what the exact quantity was, but at any rate it wasn't a significant quantity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Some soldiers also stayed behind; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the soldiers and equipment became part of the VRS's Birac Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Since a decision had already been reached to establish the Army of Republika Srpska. Everything became part of the Army of Republika Srpska, and this equipment was kept by the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your SJB carried out some of its activities in co-ordination with military organs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At first it was with the Territorial Defence and later, when the Army of Republika Srpska was established, with the members of the Army of Republika Srpska acting either in concert or co-ordinated action.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, could we have 65 ter 1D02348.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, as we're waiting for the English, this is a report you sent to the Romanija Birac CSB on the 6th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in the English and the third paragraph of page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see here in the second paragraph in the English: "The public security station co-ordinated its activity and performed it jointly with organs of the army, particularly when those carrying out the activities were persons who were directly engaged in war operations." That's correct; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 3 in the English and 2 in the B/C/S, the last paragraph, we read in pertinent part: "We deem that the level of co-operation and a joint action by employees of the public security station and members of the army is satisfactory ..." So at the time you were satisfied with the level of co-operation between the SJB and the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Our objective was to establish institutions, just as the Army of Republika Srpska wanted to do. So these institutions should function headed by the Main Staff in accordance with procedures that were in force because from the point of view of public security and safety that was the only way to operate, and also from the point of view of the Army of Republika Srpska, to have successful defence against the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, looking at the previous paragraph, we see a discussion of curbing and preventing crimes by members of the army and the note that related to this, 30 reports and other notices were submitted. Those reports would have been submitted to the VRS when the offences were believed to have been committed by members of the army; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's try and go beyond assumptions. If you're information indicated that members of the military had committed crimes, you would turn that information over to the military, like we see described here; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. At first before the military police started function or, rather, the crime prevention service within the Army of Republika Srpska, we were the ones who recorded these crimes committed. And then when this service was established in the VRS, all of these cases that have to do with soldiers, members of the VRS, were referred to them, to the crime prevention service of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That was because crimes committed by members of the VRS at that time were in the jurisdiction of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. But these institutions hadn't started functioning officially yet. As soon as that happened, we had a meeting and we referred all these cases to the military service that was in charge. And later, on the system functioned as follows. If the police would notice that members of the VRS were committing certain crimes, then they would notify the military police of that and they would take measures as envisaged by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in fact, you've said in one of your interviews that the VRS would complain if you got involved in dealing with crimes by members of the VRS. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I would just explain that. In order to prevent any kind of clash in terms of jurisdictions, we acted in accordance with that we referred all cases to the VRS, those cases that they would be in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that meant that if you believed a crime to be in jurisdiction of the army, you didn't investigate; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the later period we did not investigate. We would just hand over all the information we had to the VRS or, rather, the crime prevention service of the military police of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to go back now briefly to a couple of the points we addressed last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And before I do, actually, I'll tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D2348 receives number P6878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6878 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd ask that we call up 65 ter 06393.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We discussed last week what would be done with policemen who were believed to have committed crimes and their provision to the VRS. In fact, the minister of the interior had ordered that such policemen be placed at the disposal of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And looking at this document, this is an order from Minister Stanic dated the 23rd of July, 1992. It says at the top that this order arose out of the: "Session of the collegium on 23 July 1992," among other things. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now last Thursday we discussed the collegium of the chief of the CSB. Did the minister also hold collegiums in which he received information from the CSB chiefs?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's subordination in the Ministry of Interior. The minister when necessary would convene this collegium of the minister, that's what it was called, and it was attended by all chiefs of the centres of the security services and also advisors to the minister. So this was a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this order reflects the minister's policy that we discussed a moment ago, the policemen who committed criminal offences should be placed at the disposal of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now point 2 explains who's responsible for the execution of the order including, chiefs of public security centres. Now, you implemented this order in Vlasenica by making officers who had committed crimes available to the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 06393.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 06393 receives number P6879.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6879 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Next, sir - and I'm done with this document - we spoke last week about some log-books and criminal registers kept in Vlasenica. I'd like to try and be a little bit more specific about the ones that existed. First, the police kept a disciplinary register where disciplinary violations by members of the police were recorded; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where all these records are kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, there was something called a K log-book kept in the police station recording criminal cases before those cases were handed over to the prosecutor's office; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's the K log-book, that is to say, the crime log-book where all the crimes are logged regardless of whether the perpetrators are known or unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the prosecutor's office kept a KT log-book for known perpetrators cases, and a KTN for unknown perpetrator cases; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the prosecutor's office also had a log-book of their own; that is to say, once we as a police would deal with a criminal report, then we would have it hand it over to the prosecutor's office. On the basis of this information that we had submitted, the prosecutor can accept that report, ask for additional information, or reject it all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's the prosecutor's log-book that you confirmed last week had no mention of prosecutions of Serbs for crimes against non-Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That was the log-book of the prosecutor's office and this was taken out of context. Only the part that had to do with the seizure of weapons. However, there were many other crimes there, 180-something criminal reports that were filed. I don't have the structure of these crimes here right now, but it is certain that all of that was filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at one of the reports you sent about crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31547.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a report you sent to the Romanija Birac CSB on the 25th of September, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it discusses crimes and other violations by members of the police; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Looking to the third paragraph, it reflects eight criminal reports against members of the police. Now, none of those were filed for crimes against non-Serbs, were they?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say exactly right now, but eight criminal reports were filed. Armed robbery, things like that. Anyway, it's within that domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And these were mostly thefts and robberies, that type of crime; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think most of them were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 31547.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 31547 receives number P6880.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31509, page 189.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is the transcript of one of your interviews. And you were asked beginning at line 23 after looking at the document we've just seen, now P6880: "With regard to all of these crimes and transgressions, were any of them for actions taken against non-Serbs?" And you responded: "See in, in regards to criminal reports [sic], no." Now, does that refresh your recollection as to whether any of the eight criminal reports filed against police officers in Vlasenica in the summer of 1992 were filed for crimes they committed against non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's very difficult to speak about that now, but let's say if a policeman committed a robbery, and most frequently they would loot Muslim property, then it could have happened that a report was submitted on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say it could have happened. You're not aware of any reports filed against police officers for crimes against non-Serbs, are you?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall any crimes specifically at that time. Perhaps there was some open investigations, but I don't believe that the final result then was a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to talk now, sir, about some of the crimes committed against non-Serbs in Vlasenica in 1992. After the take-over, on the 21st of April 1992, some non-Serbs were killed in Vlasenica town; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking of the 21st of April, there were no casualties on that date. The casualties happened at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm asking specifically about killings in Vlasenica town after the take-over. There were such events; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as I said, the actual act of the take-over on the April -- on the 21st of April, 1992, there were no casualties. The casualties occurred later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And again, after the take-over property owned by non-Serbs in Vlasenica town and in the municipality was looted; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this did happen. We tried as much as we could to prevent this from happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Vlasenica town mosque was destroyed in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And specifically August of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it was destroyed by engineering units of the VRS, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the explosive was planted by somebody who obviously knew how to handle explosives.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat the last part of your answer for the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to place explosives, the person must know how to handle that. The person who were trained to do that were members of the engineers units. Now, I don't know where they were from, from which forces they came from, but I assume that they were part of the engineers units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in fact, the Vlasenica SJB was given two or three hours advance notice that the mosque was going to be destroyed; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were informed two or three hours before that certain activities would happen, and we informed the population accordingly, asking them to leave that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were informed by the VRS that the engineering unit was going to destroy the mosque; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be sure who I got the information from, but I think the information came from some unit of the Army of Republika Srpska. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just so the record is absolutely clear, they told you it was going to be the engineering unit that did the demolition; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that the mosque would be blown up in the afternoon and that we should inform the inhabitants this is the information that we received and that we were aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To your knowledge, nobody was ever prosecuted or punished for blowing up the mosque; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We recorded it in our reports as being perpetrated by an unidentified perpetrator, and the actual event did not result in any significant investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, one of your previous questions where you sought specifically to receive an answer to the engineering unit as being the one which was announced to -- to do the job, was not answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I thought it was answered at page 18, line 6. But I'm happy to re-ask the Chamber if it suits the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. Well, I see on lines 7 and 8: "Yes, we were told ..." And then the specific point you raised in your question could be covered by the yes but certainly does not appear in the explanation then given.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. I'll re-ask the question. I'd request that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question after Madam Registrar has announced that we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Have you ever considered to lodge any protest against what clearly was an announcement of the destruction of a religious -- a religious monument? Yes, Witness, have you received translation of the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll repeat the question for you. Have you ever considered to lodge any protest against what clearly was an announcement of the destruction of a religious monument?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, at that point in time, our goal was to inform the population to avoid anybody getting hurt in the immediate vicinity, so we did not have time to write any kind of protest. That means that we reduced our activities to those that were in our remit: The care for the security of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the population not be best protected by preventing the destruction to take place at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, at that point in time the only possible thing was to do exactly what we did: To inform the citizens. All other activities would not have yielded any results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then specifically ask you: If you would have gone there and would have told anyone that was about to place explosives that it may be a crime to intentionally destroy a religious monument, why do you think that would have had no effect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that point in time, we didn't have access to that building, and we didn't specifically know which persons were going to commit that act.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you can go all around the mosque and tell everyone what's going to happen in two or three hours, and you say, "Well, we couldn't look as who was preparing the explosives at the mosque." Is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we did not have access to the building. We had information that the explosion would happen, so we wanted to inform and remove the population from the area to make sure that they would leave and that they would be safe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why didn't you access to the building? Just open the door and when it's locked, then force your way into it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not consider that option in view of the fact that we were not part of those activities. We just acted pursuant to the information, and we acted within our powers to protect the inhabitants as much as we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And your powers did not include preventive action in order to avoid that crimes are committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that did include preventative action in any case. Police work also includes preventative actions, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, I do not understand that it was not within the remit of your powers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right at the beginning, we were clarifying things in order to prevent conflict of authority among the institutions. We assumed that this was something that was being done by members of the engineers unit. Then us interfering in that action would constitute a conflict of authority and powers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It being done by members of the engineers unit, would that make it any less a crime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it would not make it less of a crime, but the institutions functioned each in its own area of responsibility and authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you'd say if a clear announcement is made that the army intends to commit any act which, at face value, would be a serious crime, you would just say stay out of the way because a crime will be committed? That's your position.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, I'm talking about a conflict of powers here. There's the institution of the army, the institution of the Ministry of the Interior. Any interference in the authority of the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've told us that before. I would invite to you answer my question, that was that if the army makes an announcement that within a civilian area they are about to commit what at face value seems to be a serious crime, that the only thing you do is to say to the population stay out, stay away, I have no access to the mosque, although you can open the door. But that's your position, that that's the appropriate thing to do at that point in time. Is that how we have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At that point in time, from the point of view of the Ministry of Interior, all we could do was inform the population that they should get out of the way. We were able only to work on the aspect of the safety of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- if the army would have announced that they would kill three civilians on the market-place, would you also have gone there and say to all the public, "Stay away, because you might be hit by a bullet when the army is executing three civilians"? Would you have done the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are hypothetical questions, and we could continue with that endlessly, but what we're talking about here is that it was our task and the only option to do what we did. Had we had the information before, a day or two before, I probably would have informed along the professional line the minister about it, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I'm looking at the clock. Perhaps I should invite you not to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm in the Chamber's hands, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many -- where are we as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd estimate about half a session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half a session. Then we'll take a break first. Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back after that break, and you may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom. There was one preliminary item about a translation, I think. Perhaps so short that we could deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The Prosecution advises that it has received the B/C/S translation for -- sorry, for MFI P6713, 65 ter 31192, which was marked for identification through Witness Indjic on the 3rd of September 2014 at transcript page 25179. The translation has been uploaded into e-court under doc ID R0116819RED B/C/S. If the Defence are in agreement the Prosecution requests or will request that the Court Officer be instructed to attach the translation and that the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I hear from the Defence. My recollection doesn't tell me right away whether it was only the translation that caused the document to be MFI'd. My colleagues confirm that that was the only reason. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the only reason, then the Registrar is hereby instructed to attach doc ID R0116819RED B/C/S to document P6713, MFI'd. Once it has been attached, P6713 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, since we have mother moment, we've been informed that at transcript page 27642, line 14, on Thursday, 65 ter 31516 is recorded as having been admitted as Exhibit P6873 when, in fact, it has been admitted as Exhibit P6872. So for the clarity of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. 27642, line 14. Yes, Madam Registrar, could you please verify whether the transcript is accurate. We are talking about 65 ter 31516, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And whether it, indeed, is admitted as exhibit number P6872.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. 65 ter 31516 should have been assigned number P6873 which is assigned so in e-court for that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's ... first of all, we switch off all unnecessary microphones. I think what Mr. Traldi was hinting at is that it should have been admitted as P8 -- 6872 and that the transcript reads that it was P6873 which is inaccurate, if I understand you well, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's correct and that's the information we, and I think also the Chamber, have received from the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then this will be verified. Madam Registrar, if Mr. Traldi made a mistake, then you'll certainly draw the attention of the Chamber to that fact. If not, 65 ter 31516 is recorded now as being admitted as P6872. Witness, our apologies for dealing with administrative matters when you entered the courtroom. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, a number of Muslims who were arrested in late May and early June 1992 - Muslim civilians - were brought to the Vlasenica police station; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were aware at the time that some of the civilians who'd been brought there were beaten; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look. There's a reference to beatings, mistreatments. I heard about that only later through the electronic media, through different witness statements. However, from the 2nd of May, 1992, the police station really tried to work and to act in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure. From the 21st of April until mid-May, say, the 20th of May, it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, Witness, I'll stop you there. The question was about your awareness of some of the civilians being taken to the Vlasenica police station, that they were beaten. Were you aware at the time? I take it from your answer that you only learned about it later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That answers the question. If Mr. Traldi has any further questions on the matter, he'll certainly put them to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31509, page 245.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this will be another portion of one of your suspect interviews.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat the page number again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, page 245.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're being asked about civilians brought to the SJB here. And at the top of the page, beginning at line 3, you're asked: "All right. Were you aware of any mistreatment of these Bosniak civilians when they were brought in for interrogation?" You replied: "See, I personally did not see that someone was being harassed. But if I happened to hear from someone that someone was harassed, I insisted that this should not have -- should not be happening. And I requested from the duty policeman at the entrance to make a record of any person coming in and to write a short -- a short description and also to make a record when the person was -- when the person left the premises or ... for this reason, of the possibility of misuse by the responsible individuals. So this functioned in such a way." Then you were asked: "Okay. When you say 'harassed,' were you also aware that on -- at least on some occasions the civilians who were brought in were also beaten?" And you answered: "See, I heard about this and I took measures right away." Now, that's the truth what you said in your suspect interview, that you did hear at the time that civilians were being beaten in the Vlasenica police station; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I intervened immediately in order to have this situation overcome because, in fact, proper authority was established in the station only the second half of May 1992. Basically until then, various paragroups would barge in and it's possible that such incidents occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I take you back to one of your previous answers. When you were asked about your awareness of people being beaten when brought in, you said: "Well, look. There's a reference to beatings, mistreatments," and "I heard about that only later through the electronic media, through various witness statements ..." That wasn't true. You learned about it right away and it was not a truthful answer. Do you have any explanation as why you told us that you only learned it through the electronic media, whereas you now tell us five minutes later that you were aware of it and that you immediately took action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, people were saying that there were certain incidents and I did not see any of that. However, I acted by way of prevention and took measures with a view to prevent such situations from happening. Later on in the electronic media as I followed statements made by different witness, I came to realise that, indeed, such things had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question that was put to you was just about awareness. Now you were told -- you were told at the time that this happened, and even in one of your answers today, you said if it was reported to you then you took action. Let me just remind you that at least that answer, that you learned about it only later, is certainly not the whole truth as you were asked to tell us. Could you please keep that in mind not to seek evasive answers but to directly answer the question what is -- that is put to you. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In terms of the actions you took, you informed your superiors at the CSB of what you'd heard; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the policemen that were suspected to have participated were sent to the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Measures were taken, those that were in envisaged under the law at the time, and this was based on the agreement already reached between the Main Staff of the VRS and the Ministry of Interior towards the end of July 1992 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to come closer to the microphone, says the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, you're being asked to move towards the microphone so the interpreters can hear you more clearly. Now you said this was based on an agreement in late July 1992. Is it your evidence that measures, the transfer of these policemen to the VRS that were suspected of having beaten people at the SJB, were taken after that agreement was in place?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even before that, many measures were taken. That is to say, policemen from the reserve force were dismissed, those who acted against the law if I can put it that way. But at any rate, this agreement was reached between the Main Staff of Republika Srpska and the MUP that all paramilitaries be disbanded, handed over to the VRS, and expelled from the areas where they were operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I again take you back to one of your previous answers. When I asked you about the answer you'd given previously, you said, explaining your previous answer, you said: "At that moment, people were saying that were certain incidents and I did not see any of that. However, I acted by way of prevention and took measures with a view to prevent such situations from happening." Later on in the electronic media you said you came to realise that indeed such things had happened. From the answers you just gave, it appears that you knew already at the time that such things were happening and that you did not only act in way of prevention but that you also acted in a different way, acting upon reports, taking measures perhaps to prevent such situations from happening again but not prevent such things from happening only later finding out that they had happened. I again have to warn that you should speak the whole truth. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clear. And I am telling the truth. That is to say, at that moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I just asked you whether that's clear to you and you said it was. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the reserve policeman at the Vlasenica SJB at the time, Predrag Bastah, has been convicted after the war in Bosnia of crimes against humanity for abusing prisoners at the SJB in late May and beginning of June 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the name of the policeman again?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Bastah, B-a-s-t-a-h.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm now going to ask you about the take-over of Zaklopaca on 16 May 1992. Zaklopaca was in the municipality of Milici at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in that newly established municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You heard the next day that 60 to 80 civilians were killed during the take-over; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the next day I heard that an incident had taken place there in Zaklopaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you heard that 60 to 80 Muslim civilians were killed; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this was a crime; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this incident encouraged Muslims to leave the area of Vlasenica and Milici, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's when the intensity of moving out was on the rise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now when you explain in your statement why Muslims left Vlasenica municipality, you don't mention that they started to leave in greater numbers after other -- sorry, after other Muslim civilians were massacred. You don't mention that in your statement, do you?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I did not deal with that problem because it was within the scope of work of the Milici municipality; that is to say, a different socio-political community.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And because it was within the scope of work of Milici municipality, it would have been their SJB, not yours, that was responsible for investigating a crime; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To your knowledge, no one was ever prosecuted or punished for that crime, were they?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just for the clarity of the record, that's yes, no one was punished; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now whether they did carry out investigations, I don't know. But I know what the epilogue is: No one was punished.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about a mass murder outside of Nova Kasaba in May 1992. About 25 Muslims were killed there; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found out about that later too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say "later," this was on television within a day or two it happening; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the victims were being taken out of Bratunac by bus escorted by the Bratunac police?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: They were killed by paramilitaries from a group called the Vukovar Detachment; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also on the basis of certain knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you never saw a report or a bulletin about this crime, did you?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, this crime hasn't been prosecuted either, has it?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know. But again, I'm saying that that was under the Milici police station. Now whether they took certain measures, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: There were a number of take-overs of Muslim villages in Vlasenica in late May 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The -- a battalion of the VRS Birac Brigade took part; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are two periods. In this first period until sometime in June while the JNA was there, in the villages that were being disarmed, the newly established Territorial Defence took part as well as the units of the JNA. Later on when the Army of Republika Srpska was established, there were certain activities in accordance with the plan of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You just said June -- or the JNA was there till June. You testified earlier today that the Novi Sad Corps left on May 19th and its equipment and personnel that stayed became part of the VRS Birac Brigade. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the way these operations would work would be that people would be called with megaphones to come to a certain spot in the village to surrender their weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say, when we are speaking about the Territorial Defence and the JNA, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And also the VRS; right? After May 19th.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Territorial Defence was abolished and the Army of Republika Srpska was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, police officers from SJB Vlasenica would make a list of the weapons that had been surrendered and take them away; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the task of the police. Since the police keep records of weapons, then these collected weapons were supposed to be recorded and stored in a certain storage area in the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To ensure the police were there, the army would inform your SJB by fax the day beforehand; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's this period until the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And during the operation, the army would call the police by radio to come take the weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said you were notified by fax until the 19th of May. How were you notified when it was the VRS conducting the operations?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later when the VRS was established, institutions were established of the VRS and the Ministry of Interior. Then on the basis of requests and when necessary, the VRS would send a request to us stating that they needed certain forces, some policemen. My task was to ask the Ministry of Interior, the chief of the centre, for approval and to send these policemen who would then be placed under the command of the military unit in charge in the place where they would be stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say placed under the command. The technical term for that is resubordinated; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to discuss one such take-over in particular, the take-over of Drum. That was at the very beginning of June 1992; right? I see you've nodded but you have to articulate your answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As for the village of Piskavica Drum and the take-over there, there was this operation carried out on 29th of April that was carried out by the Territorial Defence and the Army of Republika Srpska. The other activity took place sometime in the beginning of June. I cannot say exactly. The police did not take part in that. However, later on, I acquired some concrete information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the activity in the beginning of June, that was a VRS operation; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly whether the activity was the activity of the VRS or paramilitaries, because at that time they still existed in the territory and their aim was to loot and so on and so forth. On the following day I did hear, though, that an incident had taken place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here this is again part of one of your suspect interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I think actually for the clarity of the record if we could have the previous page. And not to be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you can see that you're being asked here about the incident in Drum. Looking, beginning at line 29, you're asked -- sorry, beginning at line 24: "Did you investigate this killing incident?" And you say: "See, a report was made about this but it was very difficult to find out any information about the perpetrators." You were asked: "Who did you submit the report to?" You answer: "I forwarded the report to the centre what happened, that there was this incident."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As we do, "the centre" refers to the CSB Romanija Birac; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, beginning here with your answer at line 6, you say: "I didn't take to him. I informed him and it was requested for this case to be investigated." You are asked: "By who?" And you say: "But usually any act, if we had possibilities, we tried to document for it. But I don't think we were able to do anything special on this issue because the intensive fighting started. So this was more or less -- we tried to talk to the military police, for them to get involved in it ..." Now, that was the truth what you said in your suspect interview; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the military police that you talked to were from the Vlasenica Battalion of the Birac Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'd put to you you were informing them because your information indicated that the military had been responsible for this operation. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true, the police did not take part in this. It was either the army or the paramilitary. So we moved along in two tracks in order to try to find the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to some questions about Susica camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question for the witness. Were the paramilitaries also within the competence of the military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The paramilitaries remained after the formation of the Army of Republika Srpska. These were groups that did not wish to join the Army of Republika Srpska and they still insisted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that the military police would not investigate them because they were not subordinated to the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We also tried to inform the military police and we also tried to carry out certain steps in order to find out who committed this. Because as I say, the paramilitary groups definitely existed until the 27th or the 28th of July when the decision was made to subordinate all groups of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who would then investigate in the meantime any crimes committed by the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As an institution as the Ministry of Interior we recorded all such occurrences and conducted investigations to the extent that we were able to at that point in time. However, the Army of Republika Srpska in their investigating institutions were the ones to whom we forwarded all the criminal reports that we believed would fall under their jurisdiction. So we also tried to do it in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So sending to the military police meant that you considered it at least likely that the military -- that it was useful to investigate whether the military were responsible for the incidents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would look to see if they were members of any of the already-formed units, in which case we would then seek to have the army activated in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what did you find out about the incident Mr. Traldi asked you about, as to who were most likely the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't get very far. I've already said that. We conducted the on scene investigation, established the facts, and then opened an investigation marking it as an unidentified perpetrator. So as far as the public security station is concerned, that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, you found it useful to send all your information to the military police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As I said a few moments ago I'm going to turn to Susica camp, and first I want to clarify one point in your statement. In paragraph 50 you discuss activities to transfer Muslims from Susica to Bijeljina. When you say Bijeljina, you mean Batkovic camp; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Batkovic camp was run by the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, were you ever at Susica yourself?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Nee" [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I did not consider that a camp because it had its humanitarian nature as well for a certain period. Then I personally did not agree about the existence of any camp in the Vlasenica area, so I took some measures at different levels in order to have that thing transferred out of there and to have those people sent, if we're talking about civilians, to send them to the Federation, or if they were prisoners of war to send them to Batkovic. Because that is from where the exchanges were carried out later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you say at first that you didn't consider it a camp because it had its humanitarian nature as well for a certain period. And then you say that you did not agree about the existence of a camp in the Vlasenica area. So you'd agree, wouldn't you, that even if wasn't a camp at first, it certainly became one?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later pursuant to a specific order it became defined as a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the order you discuss in your statement from Svetozar Andric on the 31st of May, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll need about another ten minutes with the Chamber's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just asked for the time report, Mr. Traldi. You apparently read my mind. I'll first wait for the result. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the warden there, Veljko Basic, was a retired police officer who was mobilised into the TO; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Susica facility, which had been a TO facility, came under the control of the Birac Brigade when the VRS was formed; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have Exhibit P193.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an assessment of the guards service, and it's dated June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If could we have page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an assessment of the danger to buildings in Susica from attack on them. Do you agree we're discussing the same buildings, the same Susica facility you describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The analysis is a result of the order that we mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 4, the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a note about the impossibility of any disinformation or cover-up measures, and it mentions the number and structure of prisoners. It's referring to them as prisoners because by this time clearly it was a camp; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 9 in the English and 8 in the B/C/S, Major Slobodan Pajic is issuing a directive on the work of guards support. Directing your attention to point 9, he writes: "Regarding any unclear matters, contact the prison warden, chief of the Vlasenica SJB, and the 4th Battalion Vlasenica Command." Were you contacted by the guards at Susica camp about any unclear matters?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is here because in the event of an attack or any problems in the building, in the camp, all these institutions would have to be informed because they are the ones that could provide help and protection. So the guards were not obliged to report to or inform the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Setting aside their obligations, you did hear in 1992 about beatings and killings at Susica; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did find out that there were some incidents and such situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You reported those to CSB Chief Cvijetic; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you didn't investigate them because you believed them to be in the jurisdiction of the army; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you did inform the VRS of these incidents; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to the departure of Muslims from Vlasenica, I'll just have one brief question. By the time the mosque was destroyed in August 1992, almost all the Muslims were gone from Vlasenica; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you mention in your statement the municipality issuing documents on the -- on certificates for leaving the municipality. The reason Serbs had to get such a paper was to prevent them from avoiding military service; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. They had to have a certificate from the Secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As Muslims left the municipality, other Serbs moved in; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The intensity with which the flow of Serbs arriving from other locations varied, but by that time, there was already a considerable number of refugees there from other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And a body in the municipality assigned them to abandoned houses and flats; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A decision was reached - I don't know what the document was called - a commission was formed, which was now temporarily assigning abandoned apartments and houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finally, sir, on the 22nd of October, 2002, you stopped working in the police because you were not certified by the International Police Task Force, or IPTF; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this was because based on a review of your war time record and the information available to them, they had information suggesting that you'd sent persons detained at the Vlasenica police station to the Susica camp; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what was said in the reasons, statement of reasons, but I did not have the opportunity to prove otherwise, and -- or to disprove it, so that this sanction is still in force to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Just managed to get -- to stay within the two and a half hour's estimate. We'll take a break first before -- Mr. Stojanovic, before you'll re-examine the witness if at least there's any need to re-examine the witness. Is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I will require about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take those ten minutes after the break. And your next witness is stand by?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, the Chamber has been informed about some problems you have with the uploading into e-court of some of the documents in relation to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't say that we're very happy with it but let's work on the basis of hard copies exceptionally and then later on the documents will be uploaded into e-court. I do understand that the booths have received hard copies of everything you want to use and that hard copies are available for the Judges as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, let's not make too much fuss about it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can inform you that we did our part. So the Tribunal staff was not able to upload it into the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I then -- we know what the time-limits are and that might have come a bit late. But, again, let's try to avoid it to happen again, but let's work on the basis of what we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, are you ready to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours, one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Good day.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I have just a few questions that I would like to put to you. In the cross-examination you talked about how on the 19th of April 1992, immediate danger of war was declared in the Vlasenica municipality. What I want to ask you is this: Could you please tell us who made the decision to declare the immediate danger of war?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was made by the Crisis Staff on the basis of their assessment of the crisis situation. Already in that time the institution's either executive power or judicial ones did not operate. The situation was more difficult and the interethnic relations were not good.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I can just ask you to repeat the last sentence because it was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interethnic safety, security was disrupted, interethnic relations. And the institutions did not function, the judiciary and the executive bodies were not functioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the only question you asked the witness is who took that decision. Paragraph 17 of the statement reads: "The decision on declaring immediate threat of war was made by the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Vlasenica." Why ask the witness what is already in his statement you have tendered yourself into evidence? Try to be focused.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That was just a queue for what the witness had already spoken about. Could we now please have P6874 in e-court. P6864 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document. It's in front of you, Mr. Witness. I shall put a question to you related to this document.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph II of this decision on imminent threat of war, there is a reference inter alia to these reasons that you had referred to, but also there is a reference to a large number of armed citizens. My question: Is that your knowledge, namely, that in April 1992 in the area of the municipality of Vlasenica there were many armed citizens?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a large number of armed citizens because weapons were procured in different ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you spoke about the decision on disarmament of the members of the public security station in Vlasenica, active and reserve, did you receive at any point in time, in writing or orally, any kind of instructions on disarming a group of policemen as opposed to some other group on the basis of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of documents that I found at the public security station when I took over my duties, I did not come across such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the questions that were put to you today during the cross-examination by the Prosecution, you mentioned military operations or military actions. What do you specifically mean when you say "military operation"?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for military operations, at that time they were called military actions, these are activities of the Army of Republika Srpska in the areas that were in jeopardy or, rather, areas that were within their plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In these military actions, could it happen that some volunteer units could take part in the beginning of the war or paramilitary units and during the war police units as well?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would always happen up until the period when these paramilitary units were expelled. How do we put this? Planned military actions of the Army of Republika Srpska, co-ordinated with the police, they would be followed by certain paramilitary groups that committed crimes and that were out of control.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of the village of Drum, before these military activities, were there any incidents in terms of weapons being used, gun-fire being opened, lack of control in the territory of that village?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Drum is a village that is directly by the outskirts of the municipality of Vlasenica. In the previous period there was a staff there that had been established by the former chief of the Territorial Defence, Ferid Hodzic. He organised groups. Now, was it the Patriotic League or the Green Berets? And they had this location there, a check-point, and they often taunted the citizens of Vlasenica and opened fire at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The question is how you learned about that.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police patrols. We had learned that a group had been established there, headed by Ferid Hodzic who later on went to Cerska; that is to say, he became an official commander. In that period from that check-point that they used to check the Serb population, the village of Svetoke [phoen] is on the other side of Drum, very often in the evening they would use tracer bullets and fire at Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you a bit more precise on what was learned when exactly and -- because you're -- apparently are linking this to the Drum incident and therefore we need to know exactly how your questions link to what the Prosecution asked about. So could you please find detailed information on the matter rather than general information on the presence of groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, this information that you spoke of a moment ago, could you please tell the Trial Chamber when were these incidents recorded and when did all this happen?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These incidents, these provocations against Vlasenica, coming from Drum, they date back to the period even before the 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were weapons used from the village of Drum towards the town of Vlasenica after April and up until June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say, very often there were provocations, especially at night-time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us one example, some detail, about one specific provocation, what kind of provocation, what type of weaponry was used, what was done about it, whether there were any victims. Could you give us one example and to elaborate on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the most part this happened at night-time. And I've already said that the village of Drum is close to Vlasenica. There were provocations in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness, you're doing now the same as you did before: There were provocations. Give us one clear example where, at what time, what happened, what then was the response, what's the base -- the source of your knowledge? One specific example, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right now, I cannot refer to a specific date, but I know that it was repeated night after night, every night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information that you received, until when did this check-point exist? The one that made it impossible for the population to pass through the village of Drum.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the security assessment of the then-Territorial Defence of Vlasenica, newly established, there was this activity that was carried out together with the JNA on the 29th of April. Then this check-point was neutralised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I shall end with the following question: At any point in time, did you receive information as to who called the police - and from where - to speak about the activities of the -- concerning the destruction of the mosque in Vlasenica, if you know that?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall where this information came from. Was it from the command of the battalion or something similar to that, I cannot recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, thank you on behalf of the Defence. We have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Traldi, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, since the Chamber also has no further questions for you, this concludes your evidence in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. It's a long journey. And I'd also like to thank you for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I would wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next witness may be escorted into the courtroom.
